title: Module 14 · Practice Advancement
intro: Choosing an MUE, QI vs research and the IRB, PDSA cycles, reading trials (ARR, NNT, NNH, noninferiority) with real trial numbers, documenting interventions and teaching an inservice.

cases.title: Choosing a first project
cases.stem: You want one finished project in your first 6 months.

steps.q: What makes a strong first MUE topic?

options.t: A high alert, high risk, high cost or high volume drug, or one with a new safety alert
Criteria that come straight from a label or guideline, and a small enough patient number to review by hand
Whatever topic is easiest to publish, without asking leadership
options.why: Ask your manager what helps the department.

steps.q: Which kind of fix does the MUE method favor when results miss targets?

options.t: Hard wired changes: order sets, pump library limits, defaults
options.why: They work even on a busy night.

options.t: Reminder emails

cases.pearl: **Pick a high alert drug, guideline criteria, small numbers. Fix with order sets and pump limits.**

sources.t: Afanasjeva J, et al. ASHP guidelines on medication use evaluation. Am J Health Syst Pharm 2021;78:168-175
St. Mary's pharmacy leadership, IRB and P&T processes (verify locally)

cases.title: QI or research?
cases.stem: Your magnesium MUE is going well and you want to present a poster.

options.t: QI for your own hospital usually is not research, but if you plan to present or publish, ask the IRB for a determination before collecting data
options.why: Research = systematic work for generalizable knowledge with human subjects.

options.t: Posters never need IRB input

steps.q: Where can patient data from the project go?

options.t: Only inside St. Mary's systems, de identified for any presentation
Your personal laptop or email

cases.pearl: **Planning to present? Ask the IRB before collecting data. Data stays in the hospital.**

sources.t: UConn Health HSPP: quality improvement vs research
St. Mary's pharmacy leadership, IRB and P&T processes (verify locally)

cases.title: PDSA cycles
cases.stem: Your MUE found that urine output was documented on time in only 70% of magnesium patients.

steps.q: What is the IHI Model for Improvement's first question?

options.t: What are we trying to accomplish?
options.why: Then: how will we know a change is an improvement, and what change can we make?

options.t: Who is to blame?

steps.q: How do you test a fix?

options.t: A small Plan Do Study Act cycle: try it on one unit or one shift, measure, adjust
Roll it out hospital wide on day one

cases.title: Reading a trial: absolute risk
cases.stem: NICE-SUGAR: 90 day death 27.5% with tight glucose control vs 24.9% with conventional control.

steps.q: Absolute risk increase with tight control?

options.t: 2.6 percentage points (27.5 minus 24.9)

options.why: That is close to the relative increase (2.6 / 24.9).
Treat about 38 patients with tight control and one extra dies.

cases.pearl: **ARR = difference in rates. NNT or NNH = 1 / ARR.**

sources.t: NICE-SUGAR Study Investigators. N Engl J Med 2009;360:1283-1297

cases.title: Reading a trial: NNT
cases.stem: AMPLIFY-EXT: recurrent VTE 8.8% on placebo vs 1.7% on apixaban 2.5 mg BID over 12 months.

options.t: ARR 7.1 points; NNT about 14 for 12 months
ARR 81%; NNT 1
options.why: 81% is the relative reduction, not absolute.

steps.q: BRIDGE: major bleeding 3.2% with bridging vs 1.3% without. Number needed to harm from bridging?

options.why: Bridge about 53 patients and one extra has major bleeding.

options.t: About 2

sources.t: Agnelli G, et al. AMPLIFY-EXT. N Engl J Med 2013;368:699-708
Douketis JD, et al. BRIDGE. N Engl J Med 2015;373:823-833

cases.title: Noninferiority
cases.stem: RENOVE compared reduced dose and full dose DOACs for extended VTE treatment. Recurrence 2.2% reduced vs 1.8% full; clinically relevant bleeding 9.9% vs 15.2%. Noninferiority was not met.

options.t: The trial could not prove reduced dose is not meaningfully worse at preventing recurrence; it does not prove it is worse either
Reduced dose is proven dangerous

steps.q: How do you use this at the bedside?

options.t: Weigh lower bleeding against uncertain recurrence protection for each patient, alongside CHEST 2021 guidance
Ignore it

cases.pearl: **Noninferiority not met = not proven as good, not proven worse. Weigh benefits and harms.**

sources.t: Couturaud F, et al. RENOVE. Lancet 2025;405:725-735

cases.title: Documenting your value
cases.stem: Your manager asks what you contributed this month.

options.t: Interventions by category (renal dose, allergy clarified, IV to PO, duplicates, errors caught), with no patient identifiers in your own notes
options.why: Use the official system for patient level documentation.

options.t: Nothing; it is all in your head

cases.pearl: **Count what you catch. Numbers show your value.**

sources.t: St. Mary's pharmacy leadership, IRB and P&T processes (verify locally)

cases.title: Giving an inservice
cases.stem: You will teach L&D nurses about magnesium toxicity.

steps.q: Which outline works best for 15 minutes?

options.t: Why it matters (high alert), what the nurse sees first (reflexes before breathing), the numbers, the antidote, one case, 3 questions
Forty slides of pharmacokinetics
options.why: Too long for the audience and time.

cases.pearl: **Inservice: why, what you see, numbers, antidote, one case, three questions.**

sources.t: St. Mary's pharmacy leadership, IRB and P&T processes (verify locally)
